title: Asymptotic metrology with quantum-controlled causal order

collection.label: GaugeForge
collection.title: Quantum Open Problem Killer: sensing additions

question.summary: Quantum-controlled causal order improves quantum Fisher information for some noisy channels at three uses. Its advantage at large numbers of channel uses remains unknown.
question.importance: Finite-use gains from quantum-controlled order matter only if they survive as resources grow. The answer determines whether causal control changes asymptotic sensing limits or only small-instance performance.
question.unresolved: Prove that QC-QC strategies become asymptotically equivalent to parallel strategies for every smooth finite-dimensional channel family, or give a noisy family with a persistent advantage.

source.title: Reassessing the advantage of indefinite causal orders for quantum metrology
source.locator: Sec. VII, discussion of possible asymptotic advantages from QC-QC strategies
source.relationship: The source states the cataloged problem.

progress.title: A spacetime theorem identifies QC-QC as the physical target class
progress.detail: Salzger and Vilasini show that protocols satisfying their classical-spacetime and closed-laboratory assumptions are behaviorally equivalent to QC-QC. The theorem narrows the physical scope but gives no asymptotic metrology bound.
progress.label: Spacetime characterization

progress.title: QC-QC has a strict advantage at three channel uses
progress.detail: Mothe, Branciard and Abbott find noisy channel families for which QC-QC outperforms causal superpositions and fixed-order circuits at finite N. Their discussion leaves the large-N behavior open.
progress.label: Physical Review A

progress.title: Parallel, adaptive and causal-superposition strategies coincide asymptotically
progress.detail: Kurdziałek and coauthors prove asymptotic equivalence through causal superpositions. Their proof does not cover dynamical quantum control of causal order.
progress.label: Physical Review Letters

cautions.label: Finite versus asymptotic
cautions.text: The strict three-use separation proves a finite-resource advantage only. It does not determine the scaling exponent or leading asymptotic coefficient.

provenance.label: Source-stated question
provenance.note: Mothe, Branciard and Abbott explicitly ask whether QC-QC strategies can provide an asymptotic advantage after proving strict finite-use advantages.
